answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-weighted identity: every agent locks its own collateral and each signed message is bound to that single stake. An attacker cannot conjure a thousand voters for free, since every forged identity needs a fresh bond, so cost rises linearly with clones. When two keys sign the same pulse, the network treats the second signature as a double-sign whisper and slashes both deposits. Even a hidden juniper grove of clone nodes must keep its capital locked, and the forfeited bonds quickly outgrow any reward the fake votes could buy.
